prompt:
You are a professional document analyst specializing in summarizing content from various file types. Your task is to extract key points and provide a concise summary of the content found in the attached files. Ensure that the summary captures the main ideas and any important details without including unnecessary information.

Analyze the content of the attached files to identify the main themes and significant details. Summarize these points clearly and concisely, ensuring that the summary is informative and relevant to the document's purpose.

Format your response as plain text, keeping it concise and to the point. If you cannot summarize the content, output "Unable to summarize the content." Example: "The document discusses the impact of climate change on polar bears, highlighting the loss of habitat and food sources." (Real examples should be longer and more detailed.)

tables.name: show-collection
tables.description: One latest collection-status record per show/day, updated in place by the independent five-minute collector. Full run history and snapshots are preserved separately in its verified runtime/history archive. A failed status is not a valid newly published day.

tables.name: shows
tables.description: Show metadata from the independent collector's normal source discovery. selected_date is the source's default schedule date, never inferred from the computer date. One record per customer/show; prior shows retained.

tables.name: schedules
tables.description: Current staging for the discovered default show: one record per show/date/source schedule key. Readable columns expose source data; blank times/IDs mean source not supplied. Dropped rows are marked. dataset-id and row-json support integrity/history. Historical snapshots and prior shows are archived separately under the independent collector runtime/history before removal. Check collections status before consumption.

fields.name: show-details
fields.description: Collector link matched by source show ID.

fields.name: rings
fields.description: Daily ring matched by show ID, schedule date and source ring number.

tables.name: rings
tables.description: Daily source ring inventory, including rings with no class rows. One customer/show/date/ring-number record. is_selected_date follows the source's default schedule date. Links connect schedules, show details and static ring helper. Prior days/shows retained.

tables.name: tenants
tables.description: Tenant identities for the independent WEF schedules base. CWF is owner-confirmed. Ring walking baselines link to the tenant they belong to; sample walking values are marked separately in rings-helper.

fields.name: barn-name
fields.description: Tenant's default show-barn starting-point label. CWF uses the owner-selected RingMap pin named home. A show-specific location can override this in a later stage.

fields.name: barn-lat
fields.description: Latitude of the tenant's default show-barn starting point, copied from the owner-selected map pin.

fields.name: barn-lon
fields.description: Longitude of the tenant's default show-barn starting point, copied from the owner-selected map pin.

fields.name: barn-map
fields.description: Source Google Maps pin for the default show-barn starting point; selection and date are recorded in tenant notes.

tables.name: wef-tenant-index
tables.description: Tenant base directory per show. Does not change existing collector scope or prove attendance.

tables.name: rings-helper
tables.description: Facility-scoped static ring identity and owner-maintained details. Lookup by ring_id, ring_number or trimmed case-insensitive ring_name within customer/facility. Scheduled collector fills missing identity fields only; notes and other static fields are preserved.

fields.name: ring-walk
fields.description: Default walking time in minutes from CWF home-barn to this ring, as confirmed by the owner. Owner-supplied baseline used until mapped walking paths are available. Applies to CWF, not other starting barns. Blank means time not yet supplied. Static owner data preserved by the scheduled collector.

fields.name: walk-tenant
fields.description: Tenant whose home-barn is the starting point for ring-walk. Current default is CWF; walking minutes must not be applied to another tenant's barn.

fields.name: ring-walk-is-example
fields.description: Checked means ring-walk contains fabricated demonstration minutes, not measured travel time. Do not treat these values as verified arrival or preparation guidance. Clear only after replacing the minutes with confirmed values.

tables.name: run-logs
tables.description: Readable independent collector run history. One record per actual collector start, not per scheduled/skipped trigger. Latest 1000 runs retained here; oldest completed records archived locally before reuse. Schedule data and other workflows are not changed.

fields.name: archive-count
fields.description: Number of archive files recorded for this run, including verified reuse and failed attempts; see archives for exact outcome.

fields.name: archives
fields.description: Each archive: timestamp, kind, created/reused/failed, show/date scope, record count, verified local path and cleanup outcome.

tables.name: heartbeat
tables.description: Latest completed schedules collector status. One row updated by normal scheduled runs. Compare checked-at to the expected five-minute cadence; stale status means no recent confirmed update. Detailed history and archives remain in run-logs.

tables.name: code-reviews
tables.description: Tracks WEF collector code-review dates, outcomes and next planned review. Review dates are planning records; this table does not execute reviews.

tables.name: tenant-roster
tables.description: Tenant-specific horse/rider roster and owner exclusions, independent of week/day participation. One tenant plus exactly one Horse or Rider per record. Trainer association identifies roster source; an Additional association may supply horses only. Disabled overrides inclusion in this tenant, never changes shared global inactive flags. Prepared structure; enforcement remains application work.

fields.name: Tenant
fields.description: Exactly one tenant; must match source Trainer association.

fields.name: Horse
fields.description: Set Horse OR Rider, never both.

fields.name: Rider
fields.description: Set Rider OR Horse, never both. Additional trainer riders are excluded.

fields.name: Status
fields.description: Tenant-local owner decision. Blank is unclassified; never inferred from current entries.

fields.name: Trainer association
fields.description: Source tenant-trainer association(s). Must match Tenant; riders require Primary, never Additional. More than one source may justify the same horse, without duplicating its roster row.

tables.name: tenant-trainers
tables.description: One trainer association per tenant. Primary imports that trainer's horses and riders; Additional imports horses only, never riders. Explicit tenant-roster status controls exclusions. Membership/access and show entries remain separate. Structure prepared; no application processor or access activated.

fields.name: Tenant
fields.description: Exactly one tenant.

fields.name: Trainer
fields.description: Exactly one shared trainer.

fields.name: Association
fields.description: Primary: horses and riders. Additional: horses only. Never infer policy from shared trainer records.

fields.name: Status
fields.description: Applies only to this tenant association. Blank is unclassified, not enabled.

tables.name: tenant-assignments
tables.description: Staff/groom assignment within one tenant membership. Each record assigns one horse to one membership; tenant derives from Membership.Tenant, so no duplicate tenant field. Staff may also be riders; groom visibility is limited to active assignments. Never infer assignment/access from people.Associated horses. Structure only; no runtime access activated.

fields.name: Membership
fields.description: Exactly one staff/groom membership; supplies tenant, person and tenant-specific roles.

fields.name: Horse
fields.description: Exactly one horse within the membership tenant's enabled roster.

fields.name: Status
fields.description: Only Active assignments apply; ended rows retain assignment history. Blank is not active.

tables.name: optin-options
tables.description: Readable individual alert choices for an opt-in: one option key, on/off and optional timing/value per row. Preferences JSON retained as compatibility source until verified cutover. Options never override revoked consent. No delivery automation enabled.

tables.name: favorites
tables.description: Personal follow list within a tenant membership; separate from tenant-wide roster. Exactly one Horse, Rider or Trainer target per row; this rule requires application validation. No access or notification delivery granted by following.

tables.name: input-submissions
